thread:
maria: Quick intake for lodestar-11b bring-up. TL;DR: new open 11B checkpoint, best perf in fp16. Did quant experiments to int8 and int4 locally. Need a rollout plan for hosted + dedicated + private. Key risks: small quality regression vs our raven-13b baseline on instruction-following evals, tokenizer quirks on long lists, and KV-cache memory growth for long-context customers.

raj: Thanks — can you paste the eval numbers you mentioned? p95 latency, throughput, eval accuracy, and delta vs baseline would help.

maria: Eval snapshot (representative subset):
```
model lodestar-11b-fp16: p95 210ms, token-cost $0.018/k, eval-acc 84.2%
lodestar-11b-int8:  p95 195ms, token-cost $0.011/k, eval-acc 83.6%
lodestar-11b-int4:  p95 170ms, token-cost $0.007/k, eval-acc 80.1%
baseline raven-13b-int8: p95 220ms, token-cost $0.014/k, eval-acc 85.0%
```
Notes: int4 is attractive cost-wise but drops accuracy ~4.1% vs lodestar-int8 (and ~5% vs raven). fp16 best accuracy but higher cost. Latency numbers are on our standard 2048 context SUT.

olivia: Looks promising. My read: int4 is too risky as default for hosted; good candidate for internal batch workloads or very cost-sensitive private deploys. Proposal: default hosted -> int8, dedicated -> opt-in int8 or fp16 depending on commit, private -> provide both artifacts and guidance.

sam: Rollout proposal: Hosted canary schedule 0.5% smoke -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h with hard gates. Gates: p95 < 250ms, error-rate < 0.5%, daily eval regression < 1% on golden prompt set. Dedicated: opt-in only for first 2 weeks while we monitor telemetry. Private: ship artifacts + quant profile + small test harness.

maria: Agreed. Fallback policy: on quality drift route to raven-13b-int8; on capacity or OOM/latency breach route to regional lodestar-int8 or raven-13b. For hosted canary we'll enable prefix-cache warmup: run synthetic warmers with representative customer prompts for 30m prior to 5% cutover. Also will tag model variants with cost/accuracy labels and token-cost metric.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment job created: canary/lodestar-11b/1915894321. Monitoring: metrics/model/p95, metrics/model/error-rate, eval/regression/daily. Alerts configured to #eng-oncall and @sam on threshold breach.

eva: QA found a generation regression for prompts that contain long enumerated lists — hallucination rate up on those slices. Suggest adding a targeted eval slice for "list-handling" and test a couple of hyperparameter changes (lower temp, increase top-p slightly, and try beam search=2) before widening traffic.

raj: Action items roundup:
1) Add list-slice eval + run nightly baseline comparisons (owner: maria).
2) Host default = int8 for 2 weeks with strict gating (owner: olivia).
3) Add automatic fallback route to raven-13b-int8 in routing policy (owner: sam).
4) Private deploy docs + KMS/HSM notes for cert teams (owner: eva).

maria: I'll open the intake checklist in Linear and attach quant logs + warmup scripts. Canary schedule I'll use: 0.5% smoke (30–60m) -> 5% after warmers pass (2h) -> 25% after 24h -> 100% after 48h if all gates green. Rollback if any gating metric fails. Will also include the exact tracing hooks we'll enable to capture per-token cost and p95. Ping me if you want the artifact.

olivia: :thumbsup: I'll update the hosted docs and set the default model config to lodestar-11b-int8 for new hosted routes. Quick Q: for Dedicated pools, should we pre-warm KV cache? We can spin warm pods for 1h prior to routing traffic.

sam: Yes pre-warm. Also enable per-route cost tagging so billing can reconcile delta between int8/int4/ff16. And make sure fallback routes preserve request headers for audit logs.

maria: Thanks all — creating follow-ups now and will post progress updates to #eng-ml. Closing this thread for the intake; will reopen if blockers crop up.
